requirement:
`Sources::search_structure` returns the enclosing outline addresses and matched
excerpts in `matches`. The [`SearchResults`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.search.SearchResults)
field `complete` has the same meaning as for a text search.

```rust,ignore
pub type StructuralMatches = SearchResults<StructuralMatch>;
```
rationale:
The subject has two obligations. `Sources::search_structure` returns `matches` holding the enclosing outline address and the matched excerpt. Its `complete` field means what it means for text search. Per `requirements.sdk.graph.search.SearchResults`, `complete` is true when the search exhausted the scope, and reaching the exact limit still counts as complete if no further match exists. The type alias itself needs no behavioral test beyond using the type.

**Matches and excerpts.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` asserts that the match has `node.path == visible.rs` and `node.selector == "fn[visible]"`. That is the enclosing outline item.
- The same test asserts `excerpt == "call()"`. This is the matched range, which is smaller than the enclosing `fn`.
- It repeats the path check for the scoped search, and it checks the Python match path.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope]` checks the same three values (path `src/one.rs`, selector `fn[cached]`, excerpt `call()`) through the default trait implementation with an overriding provider.

**`complete` semantics.**
- `limit` of `None` with one match gives `complete == true`.
- `limit` of `Some(1)` with exactly one match gives `complete == true`. This is the "exact limit is compatible with complete" case.
- `limit` of 0 with a match available gives zero matches and `complete == false`. Both tests cover this.
- In the integration test, after a second Rust file is added, `limit(1)` gives one match and `complete == false`. This is the truncated case where more matches exist.
- With no limit, both matches are returned and `complete` is true.
- Scopes that match nothing (`hidden.rs`, `skip`, `.git`) give empty matches with `complete == true`. This is the exhausted-scope case.

Together these cover both outcomes of `complete` and the boundary at the limit, and each assertion checks the result values. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks that the type is exported. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no gaps. There are no acknowledgments.
